# Required status checks for `main` — config as code.
#
# Branch protection is configured in GitHub Settings, which means the list of
# required checks lived only in prose and drifted: jobs were added to CI that
# nobody ever added to the list, so a PR could merge with them red.
#
# This file is the source of truth. `scripts/check_required_checks.py` (run by
# `make lint`, so by CI) fails if any name here is not a real job that runs on
# pull_request, and fails if any PR check name is ambiguous across workflows —
# GitHub matches required checks BY NAME, so a duplicated name cannot be
# required unambiguously.
#
# A name listed here must ALSO come from a workflow that declares
# `merge_group:`. GitHub's merge queue evaluates required checks against its own
# gh-readonly-queue/* ref, not against the pull request, so a required context
# whose workflow lacks that trigger never reports there and every enqueued PR
# waits on it forever. No queue is enabled today; the gate enforces the rule
# now so that turning one on is a Settings toggle rather than an outage.
#
# A name may only be listed here if its workflow runs on EVERY pull request.
# Anything narrowed by `paths:` (or by a `types:` list that omits opened /
# synchronize) must stay out: when a PR touches no matching path GitHub creates
# no check run at all, branch protection waits forever for a status that is
# never coming, and that PR can never merge. The gate enforces this now, but the
# rule is the reason the docs/site checks below are commented out rather than
# listed — they are genuinely useful, just not requireable.
#
# To apply this list to branch protection (needs admin):
#
#   python3 scripts/check_required_checks.py --print-api
#
# One check name per line. Blank lines and #-comments ignored.

# --- the gates that decide whether a commit is releasable -------------------
lint
mutation
install-smoke
patch-coverage
evals

# Every matrix leg of ci.yml's `tests` job. They are listed individually
# because GitHub requires the expanded matrix name, not the job id.
tests (ubuntu-latest, 3.9)
tests (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)
tests (ubuntu-latest, 3.14)
tests (macos-latest, 3.9)
tests (macos-latest, 3.12)
tests (macos-latest, 3.14)
tests (windows-latest, 3.9)
tests (windows-latest, 3.12)
tests (windows-latest, 3.14)

# The Gherkin/BDD suite (tests/bdd, 11 features / 47 scenarios). Runs on every
# pull request and on the merge queue, same as the rest of ci.yml, so it is
# requireable by the rules above. It shipped with no CI wiring at all, which is
# the failure this entry closes: an invisible suite is one that rots.
bdd

# --- security / supply chain ------------------------------------------------
codeql-analyze
pip-audit
metadata
scan-pr / osv-scan
# The real-weights ONNX contract. Required because the failure it catches is silent:
# a model that loads and returns plausible 384-float vectors, just not the right ones.
# It fetches 133 MB from HuggingFace, cached on the pinned MODEL_REV, so a cache hit
# needs no network and an upstream outage only bites when that revision is bumped.
onnx-inference

# --- docs + site ------------------------------------------------------------
# NOT REQUIREABLE — every one of these is path-filtered, so it reports on some
# PRs and not others. Requiring them is what would brick the repo:
#
#   validate       html-validate.yml  paths: docs/**.html, .htmlvalidate.json, …
#   markdown-lint  markdownlint.yml   paths: **/*.md, .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc, …
#   theme-lint     theme-lint.yml     paths: style/**, .stylelintrc.json, …
#   vale           prose-lint.yml     paths: **/*.md, .vale.ini, .vale/**, …
#
# They still run and still go red on the PRs they apply to — they are simply
# advisory rather than blocking. To make one of them requireable, widen its
# trigger to every PR (drop the `paths:` filter); adding it here without doing
# that is now a lint failure, not a silent deadlock.
#
# `sonar-analyze` (sonarcloud.yml) IS unfiltered and would be safe to require;
# it is left out deliberately so an outage of a third-party service cannot
# block a merge.
